title: 07. Concurrency: Debugging Async Code
summary: Covers The Most Common Async Bugs (With Fixes), Debugging Tools.
objectives: The Most Common Async Bugs (With Fixes)

sections.title: The Most Common Async Bugs (With Fixes)
sections.body:
```python
import asyncio

# ─── BUG 1: Forgetting await ───
async def bug1():
    result = some_async_func()   # ❌ Returns coroutine, not result!
    print(result)                # Prints <coroutine object...>

async def fix1():
    result = await some_async_func()  # ✅
    print(result)

# ─── BUG 2: Blocking the event loop ───
async def bug2():
    import time
    time.sleep(5)        # ❌ FREEZES event loop for 5 seconds!

async def fix2():
    await asyncio.sleep(5)  # ✅ Yields to event loop

# ─── BUG 3: Not handling task exceptions ───
async def bug3():
    task = asyncio.create_task(might_fail())
    # Never awaited — exception disappears silently!

async def fix3():
    task = asyncio.create_task(might_fail())
    task.add_done_callback(lambda t: t.exception() and
                           logger.error(f"Task failed: {t.exception()}"))

# ─── BUG 4: Swallowing CancelledError ───
async def bug4():
    try:
        await asyncio.sleep(100)
    except Exception:       # ❌ Catches CancelledError in Python < 3.8!
        pass

async def fix4():
    try:
        await asyncio.sleep(100)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        # Cleanup
        raise  # ✅ Always re-raise!
    except Exception:
        pass  # OK — doesn't catch CancelledError in 3.8+

# ─── BUG 5: Creating tasks without references ───
async def bug5():
    asyncio.create_task(background_work())  # ❌ May be GC'd!

_tasks = set()
async def fix5():
    task = asyncio.create_task(background_work())
    _tasks.add(task)
    task.add_done_callback(_tasks.discard)  # ✅

# ─── BUG 6: Using asyncio.Lock from multiple threads ───
lock = asyncio.Lock()
def bug6_from_thread():
    # asyncio.Lock is NOT thread-safe!
    asyncio.run(lock.acquire())  # ❌ RuntimeError

def fix6_from_thread():
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(use_lock(), loop)  # ✅

# ─── BUG 7: Nesting asyncio.run() ───
async def bug7():
    result = asyncio.run(another_coro())  # ❌ RuntimeError: loop already running

async def fix7():
    result = await another_coro()  # ✅
```

diagrams.title: The asyncio event loop
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  ready[("ready tasks")] --> run["run a task until it awaits"]
  run --> io["register the awaited I/O"]
  io --> poll["OS reports which sockets and timers are ready"]
  poll --> ready
diagrams.explain: asyncio runs many tasks on one thread by switching only at `await`. While one task waits for the network, the loop runs another. Blocking calls (`time.sleep`, `requests`) never yield, so they stall every task — use async libraries or `asyncio.to_thread`.

sections.title: Debugging Tools
sections.body:
```python
import asyncio
import logging

# ─── Tool 1: Enable asyncio debug mode ───
asyncio.run(main(), debug=True)
# Logs: slow callbacks (>100ms), coroutines never awaited, etc.

# ─── Tool 2: Set up detailed logging ───
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)
logging.getLogger("asyncio").setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

# ─── Tool 3: Event loop exception handler ───
def exception_handler(loop, context):
    exception = context.get("exception")
    message   = context.get("message")
    task      = context.get("task")
    print(f"Unhandled: {message}, task={task}, exc={exception}")

loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
loop.set_exception_handler(exception_handler)

# ─── Tool 4: List all running tasks ───
async def list_tasks():
    for task in asyncio.all_tasks():
        print(f"Task: {task.get_name()}, done={task.done()}")
        # Get the coroutine's current frame
        if not task.done():
            task.print_stack()  # Shows where task is currently awaiting

# ─── Tool 5: Slow callback detector ───
async def slow_callback_detector(threshold_ms: float = 50):
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    loop.slow_callback_duration = threshold_ms / 1000
    # asyncio debug mode will log callbacks slower than this threshold
```
